title: The Campaign of Khaybar (Muḥarram 7 AH)
app_target: 3D Seerah learning app for ages 12-25 (interactive 3D scenes; battle timeline; verse overlays)

spine_source.work: Raheeq al-Makhtum (MSA NIU English ed.), Saifur Rahman al-Mubarakpuri, trans. Issam Diab (Dar-us-Salam)
spine_source.khaybar_chapter_pages: PDF pp. 233-239 — chapter 'The Conquest of Khaibar (In Moharram, 7A.H.)'; print page numbers equal PDF page numbers (footer-verified). p.240 opens 'Sporadic Invasions'.
spine_source.citation_format: Raheeq al-Makhtum (MSA NIU English ed.), p. N

grading_note: Skeleton (0.1) graded 2026-10-26 against the spine chapter and live sunnah.com + api.alquran.cloud fetches. The draft shepherd-story entry (old KHY-014) was absent from the owned spine chapter and unverified anywhere, so the slot was re-keyed to the live-verified Khaybar march narration (ʿĀmir bin al-Akwaʿ's verses, hunger siege, double reward). No choreography may key to any entry before the owner reviews this ledger (build-khaybar task 1.5).

conventions.block_tagging: Same as badr.json: all entries HISTORY; no reflections in this phase.
conventions.honorifics: The Prophet is referenced as 'the Prophet (PBUH)' in rendered text; Companions carry honorifics at first mention per block. No figural depiction of the Prophet (PBUH) or any face.
conventions.quote_cap: Direct on-screen quotes <= 15 words; Quran fetched live from api.alquran.cloud at build time.
conventions.no_harmonization: DISPUTED entries display ranges/both versions, never merged. UNKNOWN = not yet verifiable this session; hidden by default.
conventions.secondary_sirah: Ibn Hisham/Ibn Ishaq-derived claims are cited via Raheeq or online reproductions logged in live_verification_log.

grading_policy.CERTAIN: >= 2 independent sources, at least one canonical (Quran > Sahih Bukhari/Muslim > other canonical collections > sirah Ibn Hisham/Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Sa'd, al-Tabari > modern critical works). Raheeq al-Makhtum alone never certifies.
grading_policy.REPORTED: Solid single-chain sirah/hadith detail; accurate to attribute but from one lineage or modern retelling only; rendered with no certainty implied.
grading_policy.DISPUTED: Transmitted variants conflict; app must show ranges/both versions, never harmonized.
grading_policy.UNKNOWN: Cannot be verified from owned + live sources; never rendered without user approval.

render_as_policy.solid: Canonical or >=2 independent sources; safe as primary on-screen facts, may carry direct quotes.
render_as_policy.approx: Reported or contested detail; render visually/ambiguously, quotes flagged, no Fame-of-truth framing.
render_as_policy.hidden: Do not render in current phase; visible only in an app 'scholar's mode' if the user approves.

verse_anchors.text_en_sahih: Allah has promised you much booty that you will take [in the future] and has hastened for you this [victory] and withheld the hands of people from you - that it may be a sign for the believers and [that] He may guide you to a straight path.
verse_anchors.note: Spine quotes this verse at Khaybar's opening (p.233); its paraphrase 'abundant spoils' is looser than the verified 'much booty' — render only the verified text.

verse_anchors.text_en_sahih: And [He promises] other [victories] that you were [so far] unable to [realize] which Allah has already encompassed. And ever is Allah, over all things, competent.

Those who remained behind will say when you set out toward the war booty to take it, "Let us follow you." They wish to change the words of Allah. Say, "Never will you follow us. Thus did Allah say before." So they will say, "Rather, you envy us." But [in fact] they were not understanding except a little.
verse_anchors.note: Spine quotes it before the march (p.233); also links to Bukhari 2757 (Ka'b b. Malik kept his Khaybar share).

entries.claim: After al-Ḥudaybiyyah (6 AH), the Prophet (PBUH) marched north on Khaybar in Muḥarram 7 AH: a fortified Jewish oasis whose leadership had joined the coalition against Madinah and harboured the intrigue behind the Trench and Banū Qurayẓah.

sources.quote: hotbed of intrigue ... triggered Banu Quraiza treachery
has hastened for you this [victory]

entries.notes: Context beat for the opening card. 'Part of tripartite coalition' phrasing kept off-screen; spine wording only.

entries.claim: The Muslim force was 1,400 men with 200 horsemen; a horseman drew three shares, a footman one.

sources.quote: 1400 men ... 200 horsemen
the horse gets two shares and the foot-man one share

variants.note: No Khaybar-specific '1,400' hadith exists on sunnah.com (searched); the 1,400-with-Ridwan hadiths (e.g. Bukhari 4154) are al-Ḥudaybiyyah. The figure rests on the spine citing Za'd al-Ma'ad.

entries.notes: Crowd-count source: stage ≈1,400 as approximate; share rule itself is CERTAIN via Bukhari 4228 + Muslim 1762a + Tirmidhi 1554 + Ibn Majah 2854.

entries.claim: Khaybar lay about 60-80 miles north of Madinah: a fortified territory of castles and farms on high ground. The oasis sits in volcanic ḥarra country — dark basalt uplands over palm groves.

sources.quote: 60 to 80 miles north of Al-Madina ... castles, farms

variants.note: Distance band and 'volcanic ḥarra' characterization are geography, not hadith; terracing/basalt look is a design stylization keyed to this entry, not a graded fact.

entries.notes: Terrain brief for the heightfield: basalt-dark ground variant, forts on rises, palm-grove props. Fresh geography live-check (madainproject/Saudipedia) still owed before any on-screen distance label.

entries.claim: The spine's fort list — first division: Naʿīm, Aṣ-Ṣaʿb bin Muʿādh, the castle of Az-Zubair, ʿĀbi, an-Nizār (in ash-Shiqq); second division: al-Qamūṣ, al-Waṭīḥ, aṣ-Ṣalālim.

sources.quote: five castles ... three castles

variants.note: Other sīrah lists circulate with different name-sets and spellings (e.g. Naṭāh, al-Katībah as a district); only the spine's list is graded here. On-screen labels may use only these eight names.

entries.notes: Scene shows a small number of distinct forts; label only graded names. an-Nizār sits in ash-Shiqq per the spine's own gloss.

entries.claim: The order in which the forts fell differs by report; the spine itself flags the deeper conflict on the second division (Ibn Isḥāq: taken by force; al-Wāqidī: by negotiation).

sources.quote: Al-Waqidi's claim ... contradicted by Ishaq
We captured Khaibar by force

variants.note: Force-side: Muslim 1365g (Anas: 'We captured Khaibar by force', said thrice) + Ibn Isḥāq per spine. Negotiation-side: al-Wāqidī per spine p.236 (three forts by terms after the 14-day siege).

entries.notes: Direct input to choreography task 3.2: stage the spine's sequence as one staged range, never one confident order; DISPUTED shown via label, not harmonized.

entries.claim: Siege durations per the spine: az-Zubair fort ~3 days (water source cut), ʿĀbi ~3 days, an-Nizār stormed, the second division's al-Katība ~14 days; army returned late Ṣafar/early Rabīʿ al-Awwal.

sources.quote: a siege of three days ... fourteen days

entries.notes: Keep specific day-counts off-screen unless the owner approves; phase pacing may compress.

entries.claim: The army reached Khaybar at night and did not attack until morning; at dawn the cry went up: 'Allahu Akbar! Khaibar is destroyed... evil is the morning for those who have been warned.'

sources.quote: whenever he reached the enemy at night ... not attack till morning
Allahu-Akbar! Khaibar is destroyed
Fajr prayer when it was still dark

variants.note: Spine also attaches the night-march rajaz of ʿĀmir bin al-Akwaʿ and the du'ā 'O Allah! Lord of the seven heavens' (Ibn Hisham 2/329) to this beat — those grade inside KHY-014 (verses) and stay unrendered (du'ā) respectively.

entries.notes: Phase hinge (march/arrival). The morning line may render as label; quote cap 15 words.

entries.claim: The forts were taken in sequence: Naʿīm first; an-Naṭāt evacuated into az-Zubair's fort (3-day siege, water cut); ʿĀbi broken open by Abū Dujānah Sammak bin Kharshah al-Anṣārī 'of the red ribbon'; an-Nizār stormed with rams; then the second division (al-Katība, 14 days) and al-Qamūṣ.

sources.quote: Na'im was the first fort ...rams
we reached Khaibar and besieged them till severe hunger

variants.note: Per-fort sequence and prop details (rams, red ribbon, water-cut) are spine-only; the besiege-till-hunger core is canonical.

entries.notes: Sequential-siege choreography backbone; per-fort capture states follow the spine's staging as the graded range (see KHY-005).

entries.claim: The Prophet (PBUH) said he would give the banner 'tomorrow' to a man who loves Allah and His Messenger and whom Allah and His Messenger love; that night the flag was promised to ʿAlī (RA), and it was placed in his hand.

sources.quote: He loves Allah and His Apostle, and he is loved by Allah and His Apostle
the flag which was promised that night was for 'Ali

entries.notes: The standard-grant beat; on-screen quote within cap: 'He loves Allah and His Messenger, and Allah and His Messenger love him.' (13 words).

entries.claim: ʿAlī (RA) was held back by an eye ailment; the Prophet (PBUH) spat in his eyes and he was cured as if he had never had any trouble; he then received the banner and vowed to fight until they became like us (Muslims).

sources.quote: he was suffering from eye-trouble ... spat in his eyes
stayed behind with eyes inflamed
I will fight with them till they become like us

entries.notes: Label beat only; never depict the affliction visually beyond text; ʿAlī is faceless per standing rules.

entries.claim: Marḥab, a Khaybar champion, met ʿAmr bin al-Akwaʿ in single combat; ʿAmr's sword recoiled on his own knee and he died of the wound. ʿAlī (RA) then fought and killed Marḥab.

sources.quote: 'Amr's sword recoiled ... Ali killed Marhab
his sword recoiled and struck his own knee

variants.note: Canonical texts verify ʿAmr/ʿĀmir's sword-recoil death but name his opponent only 'a Jew'; the Marḥab pairing and ʿAlī-kills-Marḥab rest on the spine/sīrah (Musnad Ahmad 888 'when I killed Marhab' carries a very weak isnad per Darussalam).

entries.notes: Signature duel beat (task 3.4): stage the two combats visually; no boast dialogue rendered; Marḥab/Yāsir labels flagged REPORTED. See KHY-014 for the certified double-reward line.

entries.claim: After Marḥab fell, his brother Yāsir challenged; az-Zubair (RA) engaged and killed him.

sources.quote: Yasir ... Az-Zubair killed him

variants.note: Skeleton draft wrongly credited ʿAlī; corrected from the spine (az-Zubair). Single-source; canonical parallel not found. Nasa'i 3593 (live, Sahih) independently places az-Zubair at Khaybar with a horse (four shares).

entries.notes: Optional second duel beat; stage only if the owner opts in; if staged, label az-Zubair, not ʿAlī.

entries.claim: Al-Qamūṣ, the chief fortress of the second division, fell after the long al-Katība siege; reports conflict on the manner — Ibn Isḥāq: taken by force; al-Wāqidī: three forts yielded by negotiation.

sources.quote: Waqidi's claim is contradicted by Ishaq
We captured Khaibar by force
when the fort was opened, we came across Safiya

variants.note: Force: Muslim 1365g + Ibn Isḥāq. Negotiation: al-Wāqidī per spine. Do not harmonize; the scene may stage the siege and the fall, and the label carries the dispute.

entries.notes: Siege-phase climax; Bukhari 4211's 'fort was opened' wording supports breach language without settling the dispute.

entries.claim: On the Khaybar march ʿĀmir bin al-Akwaʿ chanted rajaz verses ('O Allah! Without You we would not have been guided...'); the Prophet (PBUH) said 'May Allah show mercy to him' and a man said martyrdom had been granted him. The army besieged Khaybar till severe hunger; at the conquest men roasted donkey flesh and the Prophet (PBUH) ordered the pots overturned and the meat thrown away. ʿĀmir died of his sword-recoil wound; when people spoke of a double reward, the Prophet (PBUH) raised two fingers: whoever said so was mistaken — he has a double reward.

sources.quote: Allah! Without You we would not have been guided
May Allah bestow His Mercy on him
he has a double reward
raised two fingers
for 'Amir there is a double reward

variants.note: Replaces the skeleton's shepherd-story draft, which is absent from the owned spine chapter and was not verified anywhere — dropped, slot re-keyed to this fully verified march narration.

entries.notes: March-beat choreography (rajaz cadence + hunger siege + pot-overturn) and the two-finger double-reward label; verse wording on screen only within quote cap.

entries.claim: The Khaybar people were allowed to remain and farm, yielding half the produce to the Muslims — the first fayʾ. Land split into two halves, 18 portions each side; the second half held a fifth (khums) for the Prophet (PBUH).

sources.quote: half the products of fruits or vegetation
I will allow you to continue here, so long as we would desire
divided Khaibar into two halves, 18 portions
they would be allowed to stay on condition

sources.ref: 1383 (live, Sahih Darussalam); Sunan Abi Dawud 3408 (live, Sahih)

variants.note: The 36-shares arithmetic with 18 to the Ḥudaybiyyah-pledge witnesses is spine-only (p.237, citing Za'd Al-Ma'ad) — REPORTED sub-detail. Spine's 'Muhammad has come' morning cry verified separately (KHY-007).

entries.notes: Reckoning-phase backbone. Also canonical: ʿUmar's wives received 100 wasq each — 80 dates, 20 barley (Bukhari 2328, live); Ibn ʿUmar 'We did not eat our fill except after we had conquered Khaibar' (Bukhari 4243, live); ʿĀ'ishah 'Now we will eat our fill of dates!' (Bukhari 4242, live).

entries.claim: Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy (RA) was among the captives taken when the fort was opened; she was brought to the Prophet (PBUH), and he freed her and made her manumission her dowry, marrying her; her wedding feast was hays at Sidd aṣ-Ṣaḥbāʾ.

sources.quote: her manumission was her mahr
her husband was killed while she was a bride
the only food we had was sawiq

variants.note: Bukhari 4200 also records Dihyah Kalbi was given her, then the Prophet (PBUH) took her in his share — that detail grades with this entry. The aṣ-Ṣaḥbāʾ sawiq stop (Asr prayer, rinsed mouths) is its own verified beat at the same site.

entries.notes: Label beat only; no depiction issues arise since no face is shown anywhere.

entries.claim: A Jewish woman roasted a sheep and poisoned it; the Prophet (PBUH) took a mouthful and stopped — the poison was in the sheep. She was asked 'shall we kill her?' and he said 'No.' When he asked her what had prompted her she said: if you were a liar the poison would not harm you, and if you are a Prophet it would not harm you either.

sources.quote: Shall we kill her? He said, No
roasted poisoned sheep was presented
I had determined to kill you
Allah will never give you the power to do it

variants.note: Name Zaynab bint al-Ḥārith: spine p.238 + sīrah only (REPORTED). Bishr b. al-Barāʾ's death and the woman's execution: spine says she was killed when Bishr died, but the canonical texts record 'No' to killing her; the execution/foreleg/'companions died' details live in weak chains (Abu Dawud 4509/4510 daʿīf; Mishkat 5931). DISPUTED — show both or hide; never harmonize. Abu Dawud 4509's comment calling her Marḥab's sister is also daʿīf.

entries.notes: Sober-history beat for the reckoning; parental-guidance framing like BADR-056. The core event may render; the fate and the name must not render without the owner's approval of the DISPUTED handling.

entries.claim: Fadak came to terms without fighting and became exclusively the Prophet's (PBUH).

sources.quote: without fight
the share of Khaybar and Fadak

variants.note: The surrender event is spine-only; the canonical texts (Fāṭimah/al-ʿAbbās claim narrations) corroborate Fadak's status as the Prophet's property after him, not the manner of its surrender.

entries.notes: One-line map beat only; keep out of the 3D scene unless the owner wants it.

entries.claim: Jaʿfar b. Abī Ṭālib (RA) and Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī (RA) with the Abyssinian-return emigrants arrived as the conquest of Khaybar concluded; the Prophet (PBUH) gave them shares although they had missed the campaign, singling out Jaʿfar's ship companions — the 'two migrations' people.

sources.quote: gave us a share
he did not give to anybody else who did not attend
O you people of the ship! ... two migrations
two migrations
He gave us shares along with those that conquered it

variants.note: Spine's '16 men sent back by Negus via ʿAmr b. Omaiya ad-Dāmarī' (p.238) is sīrah detail — REPORTED. The spine's warm line that he 'could not tell which gladened him more' was NOT verified verbatim; do not render it.

entries.notes: Warm closing beat: a return band joining after the conquest, then shares. No unverified quote.

entries.claim: Sūrah al-Faṭḥ's promise ('much booty... has hastened for you this') is quoted by the spine at Khaybar's opening, and the Prophet's (PBUH) reported dream of the believers entering Makkah with 'good after Badr' is tied by the narrations to Khaybar and the conquest of Makkah.

sources.quote: Allah has promised you much booty
good after Badr ... victory at Khaibar

variants.note: The verse-to-battle attribution is exegetical (spine pp.233, 240-241 context); render as bridge only if the owner accepts the framing. Note the spine paraphrases 48:20 as 'abundant spoils'; the verified text reads 'much booty'.

entries.notes: Bridge card toward Muʾtah/Makkah models; quote the verified anchor text only.

entries.claim: After Khaybar the Prophet (PBUH) sent a detachment to Wadi al-Qurā (a man was killed there by an arrow); the Khaybar spoils held no gold or silver — only clothes, equipment and property.

sources.quote: no gold or silver in the spoils
at Khaybar they got no gold or silver
four banners ... eleven Jews

variants.note: Spine's Wadi al-Qurā details — four banners (Saʿd b. ʿUbāda, al-Ḥubāb, ʿAbbād b. Bishr, Sahl b. Ḥanīf), 11 Jews killed one by one, ~2 days, 4-day stay — are sīrah-only (REPORTED). Abū Dāwūd 2711 also records Miʿḍam b. ʿUmr's cloak taken from the spoils (Hisma story).

entries.notes: Postscript beat; the no-gold-silver fact is a good honesty note for any spoils rendering. Keep out of the scene unless the owner opts in.
